q: What happens if an obligated plant misses its CCTS emission intensity target?
title: Missing a CCTS intensity target
short: The plant must buy and surrender carbon credit certificates equal to its shortfall, one certificate per tonne of CO2e. If it fails to surrender them, the Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025 provide for environmental compensation, set at twice the average certificate trading price for that compliance year.
audience: Plant heads and CFOs of CCTS obligated entities

ol: Your target is an emission intensity: tonnes of CO2e per tonne of product, set against a 2023-24 baseline.
After the compliance year, verified emissions are divided by verified output to get achieved intensity.
Shortfall in tonnes = (achieved intensity minus target intensity) x output in that year.
One carbon credit certificate covers one tonne of CO2e of shortfall.

ul: Buy certificates on a power exchange in the trading sessions held under the scheme.
Use certificates you banked from an earlier year when you beat your target.
Cut intensity during the year, which is cheaper when the abatement cost is below the certificate price.

p: The 2025 target rules, notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 8 October 2025 for aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper, provide for environmental compensation levied through the Central Pollution Control Board on entities that do not surrender enough certificates. The rate is twice the average price at which certificates traded in the compliance year.

Separately, the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022, carries penalty provisions for non-compliance by designated consumers. Read the gazette text for the exact amounts, timelines and whether the unmet obligation carries forward.

sections.h: What to do during the year
ul: Track intensity monthly from documented fuel, power and production, not only at year end.
Estimate your likely shortfall each quarter and budget at a range of certificate prices.
Keep monitoring records ready for verification; unverified emissions cannot establish compliance.

example.title: Illustrative example: a cement plant
lines: Target 0.80 t CO2e per tonne of cement; achieved 0.83; output 500,000 tonnes
Shortfall: (0.83 minus 0.80) x 500,000 = 0.03 x 500,000 = 15,000 tonnes, so 15,000 certificates
At an illustrative average price of Rs 500 per certificate: 15,000 x 500 = Rs 75 lakh to buy and surrender
If not surrendered, environmental compensation at twice that price: 15,000 x 1,000 = Rs 1.5 crore
example.note: The Rs 500 price is an assumption for the arithmetic only. Use the actual average trading price once the exchanges publish results.

senseible: Senseible builds a monthly record of fuel and electricity emissions from invoices and bills, each linked to its source document, which you can set against production to track intensity. It is not a CCTS verifier, does not trade certificates and does not calculate your penalty.
